§ 2Content

§ 3GERMINAL LAYERS

  • Germ layers are the embryonic tissue layers that form during early embryonic development and give rise to all organs and tissues of the body.
  • The number of germ layers is a key classification axis for animals.

Two Types of Germ Layer Organisation

#### 1. Diploblastic

  • Animals with only two germ layers: Ectoderm (outermost) + Endoderm (innermost).
  • E.g. Porifera, Coelenterata (Cnidaria), Ctenophora.

#### 2. Triploblastic

  • Animals with three germ layers: Ectoderm + Mesoderm (middle) + Endoderm.
  • E.g. Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata, Chordata (all phyla from Platyhelminthes onwards).

What Each Germ Layer Gives Rise To

  • Ectoderm — skin, nervous system, sense organs.
  • Mesoderm — muscles, bones, circulatory system, gonads.
  • Endoderm — lining of digestive tract, lungs, liver, pancreas.

§ 4Key concepts

  • Diploblastic (Porifera, Coelenterata, Ctenophora) | Triploblastic (Platyhelminthes → Chordata)
  • 3 germ layers: Ectoderm, Mesoderm, Endoderm
